# App-shell layout constraint — Library Analysis

Scope: not one component. How libraries express a full-height frame, propagate a
definite height down a nesting chain, and clip/scroll inside containers like split
panes. Covers `Stack`, `ScrollArea` and `Splitter` together, because the problem is
the chain between them.

## The problem, stated once

A scrollable region needs an unbroken chain of constraint from the viewport down.
Three roles:

| role | CSS | who plays it |
|---|---|---|
| **ceiling** | `height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden; display: flex` | exactly one ancestor |
| **conduit** | `flex: 1; min-height: 0` (and be a flex container) | every intermediate level |
| **consumer** | fill the given box, scroll inside it | the leaf |

Constraint flows one way. No consumer can repair a broken conduit above it — which
is why a missing `min-height: 0` at any level surfaces as "the page scrolls when it
shouldn't", far from its cause.

### Quick Comparison

| | Mantine | Radix Themes | Chakra UI v3 | react-resizable-panels |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Frame primitive** | `AppShell` (a *shell*, not a frame) | none | none | none |
| **Architecture** | `position: fixed` + calc'd offsets | flex, manual | flex, manual | flex |
| **Conduit vocabulary** | n/a — sidestepped | `flexGrow` + `minHeight` props | `flex` + `minH` style props | none |
| **Clip prop** | n/a | **no `overflow` prop at all** | `overflow` (style prop) | `overflow: hidden`, **non-overridable** |
| **Chain documented** | n/a | no | no | no — FAQ punts to viewport math |
| **Standout** | avoids the problem entirely | granular, honest props | everything expressible | forces the clip decision |

## Per library

### Mantine — `AppShell`
The only library shipping a dedicated full-height layout component, and it solves a
different problem: it's a *shell* (Header / Navbar / Main / Aside / Footer), not a
generic frame. Its mechanism avoids the chain outright — every section is
`position: fixed`, and `AppShell.Main` is offset by calc against CSS variables
(`--app-shell-header-height`, `--app-shell-navbar-width`). Nothing resolves against
a parent's height, so `min-height: 0` never arises.

Scrolling is explicitly inner-region: *"All AppShell components have `position: fixed`
styling, so they do not scroll with the page"*, and a section becomes scrollable via
`component={ScrollArea}`.

Verdict: an architecture, not a primitive. Buys immunity from the chain at the cost of
fixed positioning throughout — and it only works for the one canonical shell shape.

### Radix Themes — layout props, no frame
Ships `flexBasis`, `flexShrink`, `flexGrow`, plus `width`/`minWidth`/`maxWidth` and
`height`/`minHeight`/`maxHeight` as responsive props on Box/Flex/Grid.

So the conduit **is** expressible — `<Flex flexGrow="1" minHeight="0">` — but the
pattern is never named, and there is **no `overflow` prop at all**, so the ceiling
isn't expressible without an escape hatch. No app-shell recipe in the docs.

Verdict: closest to Move's shape. Same gap, one level worse (Move at least has
`fill="screen"`).

### Chakra UI v3 — everything expressible, nothing named
Full CSS-property passthrough: `overflow`, `minHeight`/`minH`, `flex`, `h="dvh"`
(with `dvh`/`svh`/`lvh` tokens). A full-height layout is `<Box h="dvh" overflow="hidden">`.
No shell/frame component; the docs cover the props, not the composition.

Verdict: maximum expressiveness, zero guidance. The chain is entirely on the author.

### react-resizable-panels — the cautionary tale
Directly comparable to Move's `Splitter`, and the community hits our exact wall:
*"The Resizable Panel Group and Panels do not seem responsive to relatively declared
heights like `height: 100%` or `min-height: x`"*. The accepted workaround in the
shadcn discussion is hardcoded viewport math — `h-[calc(100vh-72px)]`, subtracting a
header's pixel height.

Two design choices worth stealing from and one to avoid:
- `Panel` and `PanelGroup` set `overflow: hidden` **by default and non-overridably**
  (`display`, `flex-direction`, `flex-wrap`, `overflow` are all locked). The library
  takes the clip decision away from the author.
- Scrollable panel content is documented as the author's job: *"use CSS overflow prop
  along with min-height style for your panel's inner-content"*.
- The `calc(100vh - 72px)` folklore is what a missing conduit looks like in the wild.

Verdict: Move's `Splitter` (`height: 100%` on Root and Panel, `overflow: auto` on
Panel) is **better behaved than the category leader**, provided the conduit exists.

## Recommendations for Move

**1. No new component.** A generic `Frame`/`Viewport` primitive is an outlier — nobody
ships one. Mantine's `AppShell` is a shell, not a frame, and it buys its immunity with
`position: fixed`. Everyone else assembles the ceiling from a generic box plus props.
`<Stack fill="screen" overflow="hidden">` is the industry-normal form.

**2. Name the clip prop `overflow`, not `clip`.** The only naming prior art is CSS
itself: Chakra passes `overflow` through, react-resizable-panels hardcodes
`overflow: hidden`, and Radix Themes' omission of it is a documented-by-absence gap.
An enum (`visible | hidden | auto`) beats a boolean `clip`, because Move's purity gate
bans inline `style` — so consumers need a way to express `overflow: auto` on a plain
container too, not only the clipping case.

**3. Add `min-height: 0` to `Stack[data-flex='1']`.** No surveyed library defaults it —
Radix Themes makes it explicit per-instance — so this is Move choosing an opinion. Two
reasons it's the right one anyway: `Stack` already defaults `min-width: 0` on the very
same selector, so the asymmetry is the anomaly rather than the fix; and `Stack` defaults
to `column`, which makes the *unguarded* axis the common one. The accepted cost
(content can compress below its natural size with no scroller) is precisely the cost
already accepted horizontally, and the comment justifying `min-width: 0` there —
long code blocks forcing width — transposes exactly.

**4. Change nothing about the consumers.** `ScrollArea.Root`, `ScrollArea.Content`,
`Splitter.Root` and `Splitter.Panel` already hold the correct recipe. `height: 100%`
resolves fine against a `flex: 1` parent that has `min-height: 0`, and works in
strictly more parent types than `flex: 1 1 auto`, which silently no-ops in a block
parent. Swapping them would regress cases that work today — and react-resizable-panels
shows where the alternative leads.

**5. The real differentiator is documentation.** Not one of the four libraries documents
the constraint chain. Radix Themes has the props and no recipe; Chakra has everything
and names nothing; Mantine dodges it; react-resizable-panels' users hardcode viewport
math. Naming the three roles — ceiling, conduit, consumer — in the layout docs and
teaching the shell pattern in `app-setup` / `app-page` is a genuine gap in the category,
not table stakes.

### Default candidates (not decisions)
- `overflow` on `Stack`: no default (omit the declaration entirely) — confidence high;
  defaulting to `visible` would emit a redundant rule, and defaulting to `hidden` would
  break every existing `Stack`.
- `min-height: 0` under `[data-flex='1']` only, never unconditionally — confidence high.

### Key decisions needed
- `overflow` as an enum on `Stack` only, or on a shared layout prop set (Align, Grid,
  Card also plausibly want it)?
- Whether `fill="screen"` should imply `overflow: hidden`. Argument for: a viewport-height
  box that doesn't clip is the bug we started from. Argument against: it makes one prop
  do two things, and `fill="screen"` on a page that *should* scroll becomes unexpressible.
  My lean: keep them separate, and document the pair.
